title: Route Governor: staged config refactor and schema surgeon for tiered-region routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Rework the routing policy intake and validation pipeline (the 'Route Governor') so that region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variant rules are validated semantically and can be migrated gradually. Scope includes: typed AST for policies, staged semantic checks, deterministic canonicalizer, a migration shim to support old DSL shapes, and telemetry hooks for rollout.

Background: Current policy engine accepts a permissive DSL that mixes syntactic and semantic checks in the runtime dispatcher. This leads to production surprises (silent fallbacks, ambiguous region weights) and brittle migration when we introduce new tier semantics (e.g., burst-capacity tiers) and model-variant fallbacks. Previously landed work focused on lints and lightweight validators, but we need a stronger safety boundary before adding region-tier autoscaling features for Dedicated and Private customers.

Goals:
- Implement a typed intermediate representation (Typed-IR) for routing policies to separate parsing from semantic validation.
- Provide staged validation: syntactic -> type/shape -> semantic constraints -> safety invariants.
- Add a canonicalizer that normalizes semantically-equivalent rules for deterministic comparison, rollout diffs, and hashing for cache keys.
- Build a migration shim that logs compatibility warnings and provides automated transforms for existing customer configs.
- Emit structured telemetry and policy diagnostics to Console for rule-level tracing and rollback points.

Non-goals:
- Changing high-level policy primitives (we keep existing DSL surface stable for now).
- Implementing a new policy language — this is an internal refactor and safety layer.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Typed-IR vs. on-the-fly checks: Typed-IR adds upfront complexity and a compile step, but greatly reduces runtime ambiguity and allows property-based testing. Chosen: Typed-IR + caching of validated artifacts.
- Strict vs. lenient migration: We use a staged approach: warn-only for a configurable period, then opt-in strict mode per org, then global enforcement. This minimizes customer disruptions.
- Canonicalization strategy: Normalize numeric weight specs (e.g., "50%" -> float), collapse redundant rules (same region/tier pairs), and order keys deterministically. This enables deterministic diffing for Console rollouts.
- Telemetry: Emit policy_validation.{ok|warn|fail} events with rule fingerprint, validation stage, and suggested fix. Avoid exposing secrets in diagnostics.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
1) Feature branch: implement Typed-IR parser, unit tests, and canonicalizer (ENG-605414).
2) Canary: Enable warn-only validation for 5% of traffic in staging, emit diagnostics to a temporary policy dashboard (ENG-605415).
3) Migration CLI: ship a tool that suggests transforms and auto-fixes for common shape issues (ENG-605416).
4) Gradual enforcement: After 4 weeks of warn-only, toggle opt-in strict validation per org, then flip global flag.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for parser/tokenizer with invalid and edge-case inputs (sequence length constraints, missing tiers).
- Property-based tests that generate random policy trees and assert invariants after canonicalization.
- Fuzz harness keyed off real customer configs (redacted) to discover transform regressions.
- Integration tests: deploy validated policies into mock routing stack and assert dispatch decisions match specification across region and tier permutations.
- Performance: validate that compile-time overhead is acceptable (<10ms median for typical policy) and cache miss scenarios are measured.

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Validation false-positive rate <= 0.5% for existing production policies during warn-only window.
- Policy compile latency median < 10ms, P99 < 200ms.
- Telemetry coverage: 100% of validation failures emit a policy_fingerprint and stage.
- Migration CLI suggests fixes for >80% of warn-only issues automatically.

Docs & Console changes:
- Console: Rule diagnostics panel with fingerprint, canonical diff, and rollback link.
- Docs: "Routing DSL migration guide" with examples, common transforms, and security notes (link to Confluence).

APIs / GitHub / links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Route+Governor+Design+(internal)
- RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/198
- Work branch prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-governor/tree/feature/typed-ir
- Draft Console dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/policy-validation (internal preview)

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Typed-IR parser and semantic validator landed behind feature flag.
- Canonicalizer implemented with unit tests and property tests.
- Warn-only rollout tested in staging for at least 2 weeks with false-positive rate below threshold.
- Migration CLI available in OSS tools (beta) and internal docs published.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: False positives block customers. Mitigation: warn-only rollout and per-org opt-out.
- Risk: Runtime latency from compile on cache miss. Mitigation: aggressive caching, background compilation, and backpressure metrics.
- Risk: Incorrect canonicalization causing behavior drift. Mitigation: property tests and golden-file diffs against production snapshots.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish parser prototype and open ENG-605414 (Typed-IR parser + unit tests).
- Build minimal canonicalizer and add property-test harness (ENG-605415).
- Create migration CLI prototype and example transforms (ENG-605416).
